government.note: Republic of China under the 1947 Constitution and its Additional Articles. The President, directly elected by plurality since 1996, is commander-in-chief and directs foreign affairs, and appoints the Premier (President of the Executive Yuan) without the Legislative Yuan's consent. The Legislative Yuan can pass a no-confidence vote against the Premier, after which the President may dissolve it. If both the presidency and vice-presidency fall vacant, the Premier acts. On 1 January 2000 a National Assembly (elected 1996) also existed as a constitutional body; it was made an ad hoc body in 2000 and abolished by the 2005 amendments, after which constitutional amendments go to a referendum.

system.note: On 1 January 2000: the fourth Legislative Yuan, elected in December 1998 and expanded to 225 members with three-year terms, largely by SNTV in multi-member districts plus list seats. The 2005 constitutional amendments halved the chamber to 113 seats with four-year terms from the January 2008 election (parallel voting): 73 single-member FPTP seats, 6 indigenous seats by SNTV and 34 party-list seats. The schema cannot express the change of size and system over time.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the December 1998 Legislative Yuan vote: KMT 46.4%, DPP 29.6%, New Party 7.1%, Democratic Union of Taiwan 3.7%, New Nation Alliance 1.6%, Taiwan Independence Party 1.5%, Democratic Non-Partisan Alliance 0.7%, independents 9.4%. The KMT counts as liberal conservative, the DPP and the small pro-independence parties as social liberal, the New Party as national conservative; independents and non-partisan alliances go to big tent. The March 2000 presidential vote (Chen 39.3%, Soong 36.8%, Lien 23.1%) shows the KMT vote splitting after Soong's departure.
